chat.text: I'd say that having a YANG Doctors review is beneficial even when YANG Doctors are designing YANG modules. Anecdotal evidence says that the review will find issues in these cases, might as well find it as early as possible.

chat.text: Thank you Per for volunteering. More eyes is always better. We received a couple of good inputs; let us introduce those in the next version

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: @Jan, I get your point about reference to models not implemented in the controller itself. But I would imagine that the controller would be implementing the network topology model which would be calling out devices and their names in the network.

chat.author: Jan Lindblad
chat.text: @Mahesh: Very good. I expect all relevant devices to be represented in the topology, and could meaningfully be referenced there. But here we had references to components. Currently we do not have any model with all relevant components. This model is still young and incomplete, so maybe we will come up with something better than a plain string.

chat.author: Reshad Rahman
chat.text: Continue this question on the mailing list?

chat.author: Robert Wilton
chat.text: @Reshad.  Yes, always good to discuss on the list.

chat.author: Per Andersson
chat.text: Any deployment will need to sort out PKI for key rotation, expiration time of keys, rekeying etc. That would define the temporal dimensions for the signatures.

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: On the charter question, and with my AD hat on, verification state for energy telemetry in the controller model is in scope; the regulatory, renewable-attribution and carbon-accounting use cases (and modelling a grid operator's feed, issue #11) are not. Narrow the draft before an adoption poll. Anything more is a recharter conversation that Rob talked about.

chat.author: Chris Adams
chat.text:
this post here may be of interest for Toni Li ( I think was the person responding) - there are regulatory drivers of disclosure at a site level for share of clean energy, rather than an org level, and ways existing standards to tracking this, but at present, there is no agreed way to 'roll up' readings from devices, to facilities, to organisational reporting.  
I wrote a bit here about how yang handled upward aggregations, and how that may be useful for supporting declarations of the use of clean energy 
https://rtl.chrisadams.me.uk/2026/07/how-could-you-extend-yang-to-verify-clean-electricity-claims/
